subject: science
passage: The tagua palm of northern South America produces seeds so hard and white that they are known as vegetable ivory. Before plastics became common, factories in Europe and the United States ______ millions of tagua seeds every year into buttons for coats and shirts. Today a few workshops still use the seeds for jewelry and small carvings.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Turned" is the verb of the sentence, and "millions of tagua seeds" is its object—the thing that was turned into buttons. No punctuation should separate a verb from its object, so nothing goes between "turned" and "millions."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon joins two independent clauses; here it would cut the verb off from its object.
explanation.B: Correct. The verb "turned" flows straight into its object with no punctuation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A comma can't separate the verb "turned" from its object "millions of tagua seeds."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete sentence; "factories in Europe and the United States turned" is not complete without its object.
